steps: Choose the size by rider height (S, M or L).
Press the headset cups into the front tube.
Build the other parts onto it from the front to the back.
frame.signs: Cracks near the welds or a bend after a crash. Do not ride a cracked frame.
frame.where: The main body of the bike. Every other part bolts onto it: fork at the front tube, seat post in the tube behind you, cranks at the bottom, rear wheel at the back.
frame.does: Holds everything together and sets the size and riding position.

steps: Slide the fork tube up through the headset bearings.
Fit the stem on top and tighten the top cap lightly.
Align with the wheel, then tighten the side bolts.
fork.signs: Bent legs, wobbling steering, or a clicking noise at the front.
fork.where: The two legs that hold the front wheel. The top of the fork goes up through the front tube of the frame and ends under the stem.
fork.does: Holds the front wheel and lets you steer.

steps: Loosen the stem and slide it onto the fork tube.
Center the bar in the stem clamp.
Tighten the bolts a little at a time, in a cross pattern.
handlebar.signs: Bar rotates when you push on it, or grips are worn through.
handlebar.where: At the top of the fork, in front of the rider. The stem clamps to the fork tube and the bar clamps into the stem.
handlebar.does: Steering, plus a place for brake levers, grips and lights.

steps: Slide the post into the seat tube.
Set the height so your leg is nearly straight at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Tighten the clamp bolt and level the saddle.
saddle.signs: Saddle tilts, post slips down, or the cover is torn.
saddle.where: On top of the tube that rises behind the pedals. The post slides into that tube and the saddle clamps on top of the post.
saddle.does: Where you sit. The height changes how well you can pedal.

steps: Open the quick release or loosen the axle nuts.
Slide the axle fully into the fork slots.
Tighten evenly and check the wheel spins without rubbing.
frontwheel.signs: Flat or cracked tire, bent rim, or spokes that are loose.
frontwheel.where: Between the two fork legs at the front. The axle sits in the slots at the bottom of the fork.
frontwheel.does: Carries your weight at the front and rolls the bike forward.

steps: Put the chain on the smallest gear.
Slide the axle into the rear slots.
Tighten, then check the wheel is centered.
rearwheel.signs: Wheel wobbles, clicking from the hub, or a worn-out tire.
rearwheel.where: At the back, in the slots where the two rear tubes meet. The gear cluster sits on the right side, next to the chain.
rearwheel.does: Receives the pedaling power through the chain and drives the bike.

steps: Grease and slide the axle through the bottom bracket.
Press the crank arm on the axle and tighten the bolt.
Fit the other arm 180° opposite.
crank.signs: Teeth look like shark fins, or the crank is loose and clicks.
crank.where: At the lowest point of the frame, below the seat tube, where the three big tubes meet. The big gear sits on the right side.
crank.does: Turns your leg power into rotation for the chain.

steps: Find the L and R marks on the pedal axles.
Thread by hand first to avoid cross-threading.
Tighten with the wrench.
pedals.signs: Loose spin, broken pins, or a creak with every pedal turn.
pedals.where: Screwed into the end of each crank arm. The right pedal turns clockwise to tighten. The left pedal has a reverse thread.
pedals.does: Where your feet push to drive the bike.

steps: Thread through the rear derailleur first.
Wrap around the front and rear gears.
Join with the master link and test by turning the pedals.
chain.signs: Chain skips, shiny rusty links, or it has stretched past 0.75%.
chain.where: A loop from the big front gear at the pedals to the small gears at the rear wheel. The top run pulls, the bottom run returns.
chain.does: Carries power from the pedals to the rear wheel.

steps: Bolt each brake to its mount on the fork and rear tubes.
Attach the cable and set the pads close to the rim.
Squeeze the lever and check both pads hit flat on the rim.
brakes.signs: Squealing, long lever pull, or pads worn to the line.
brakes.where: Pads sit beside each rim: front pads on the fork legs, rear pads on the rear tubes. The levers are on the handlebar and are joined by cables.
brakes.does: Squeezes the rim to slow you down.

steps: Bolt the derailleur on the frame hanger.
Slide the cassette on the hub and tighten the lockring.
Connect the shift cable and tune the limit screws.
derailleur.signs: Slow shifting, skipping gears, or a bent hanger.
derailleur.where: At the rear wheel on the right. The cassette (stack of gears) is on the wheel hub. The derailleur hangs below it and moves the chain.
derailleur.does: Changes gears by moving the chain across the cassette.

steps: Wrap the rubber mount around the bar.
Point it slightly down.
Charge by USB before the first ride.
light.signs: Dim beam, will not hold a charge, or a cracked mount.
light.where: Clamped onto the handlebar, near the stem, pointing forward.
light.does: Lets you see at night and lets others see you.

steps: Mount the engine on its frame bolts.
Fit the swingarm on the pivot bolt.
Attach the fork, shocks, seat and body parts.
frame.signs: Bent tubes or cracks after a fall. Needs a professional check.
frame.where: The steel skeleton of the bike. The engine hangs inside it, the front fork attaches at the front tube, and the swingarm at the back holds the rear wheel.
frame.does: Holds all the parts and decides how the bike handles.

steps: Slide the tubes through the top and bottom clamps.
Mount the front wheel and axle.
Tighten the clamp bolts to spec and test the springs.
fork.signs: Oil leaking on the tubes, or a hard thud over bumps.
fork.where: The two shiny tubes in front of the headlight. They hold the front wheel at the bottom and connect to the frame at the top.
fork.does: Absorbs bumps at the front and lets you steer.

steps: Clamp the bar on the top clamp.
Fit grips, levers and switches.
Connect the cables and adjust the lever play.
handlebar.signs: Stiff or frayed cables, loose levers, or bent bar ends.
handlebar.where: On top of the fork, right in front of the rider. The brake lever and throttle are on the right grip and the clutch lever is on the left.

steps: Turn the fuel tap to OFF.
Set the tank on its rubber mounts and bolt it.
Connect the fuel line and check for leaks.
tank.signs: Rust inside, fuel smell, or dents that block the tank.
tank.where: In front of the seat, over the engine. The fuel cap is on top and a fuel line runs from the bottom to the carburetor or injector.
tank.does: Stores the fuel and feeds the engine.

steps: Line up the seat with the tabs on the frame.
Press down at the back until it clicks.
Or fit the two bolts underneath.
seat.signs: Torn cover, soaked foam, or a latch that no longer clicks.
seat.where: Behind the fuel tank, resting on the rear of the frame. It latches at the back or is bolted underneath.
seat.does: Where the rider and passenger sit.

steps: Lift into the frame cradle.
Fit the mounting bolts and torque them.
Connect the fuel, exhaust, wiring and chain.
engine.signs: Smoke, knocking, or loss of power. Have the engine inspected first.
engine.where: The big metal block in the middle of the frame, under the fuel tank and above the footpegs. The chain sprocket is on the left side.

steps: Pull off the plug cap.
Unscrew the old plug with the plug socket.
Screw in the new one by hand, then snug it. Do not over-tighten.
plug.signs: Hard to start, rough idle, or black or white deposits on the tip.
plug.where: On the side of the cylinder head, the top part of the engine. A rubber cap with a wire is pushed on its end.
plug.does: Creates the spark that ignites the fuel.

steps: Fit a new gasket at the engine port.
Hand-tighten the two flange nuts.
Mount the muffler bracket, then tighten all.
exhaust.signs: Rust holes, louder sound, or a leak with black soot.
exhaust.where: Starts at the front of the engine cylinder, curls down under the engine and runs back along the right side to the muffler.
exhaust.does: Carries hot gas away and lowers the noise.

steps: Bolt the housing to the brackets on the fork.
Plug in the wiring connector.
Set the beam so it does not blind oncoming riders.
headlight.signs: Bulb is dim or blown, or water is inside the lens.
headlight.where: At the very front, just above the front wheel and between the fork tubes.

steps: Lift the front of the bike on a stand.
Slide the wheel into the fork with the disc between the brake pads.
Insert the axle and tighten the axle and pinch bolts.
frontwheel.signs: Cracks in the tire sidewall, or tread worn to the indicators.
frontwheel.where: Held between the two bottom ends of the fork by the front axle. The brake disc is on its left side.
frontwheel.does: Carries the front load and steers.

steps: Slide the axle through the swingarm and wheel.
Fit the chain and adjust the slack.
Tighten the axle nut and recheck the chain.
rearwheel.signs: Bald tire, wobble, or a bent rim.
rearwheel.where: At the back, on the swingarm. The big sprocket for the chain is on its left side.
rearwheel.does: Drives the bike. Power from the engine reaches the road here.

steps: Bolt the disc onto the hub.
Fit the caliper over the disc and bolt to the fork.
Attach the brake hose and bleed the system.
brake.signs: Grinding sound, a warped disc, or brake pads thinner than 2 mm.
brake.where: The shiny disc is bolted to the left of the front wheel hub. The caliper clamps over it and is bolted to the fork leg.
brake.does: Clamps the disc to stop the front wheel.

steps: Bolt the top end to the frame.
Bolt the bottom end to the swingarm.
Set the spring preload on both to the same setting.
shock.signs: Oil on the shock body, bouncing after bumps, or a sagging rear.
shock.where: On both sides at the back, from the frame above the rear wheel down to the swingarm.
shock.does: Soaks up bumps so the rear wheel stays on the road.

steps: Fit the new sprockets on the engine shaft and wheel hub.
Loop the chain and join it with the clip link.
Adjust slack to about 25 mm and lubricate.
chain.signs: Hooked sprocket teeth, kinked links, or very loose slack.
chain.where: On the left side. Small front sprocket on the engine, big rear sprocket on the rear wheel, with the chain looped over both.
chain.does: Transfers engine power to the rear wheel.

steps: Thread each stem into the lever mount.
Tighten the lock nut.
Sit on the bike and adjust until you see the road behind.
mirrors.signs: Cracked glass, or a mirror that no longer holds its position.
mirrors.where: Screwed into the handlebar near each grip and rising up to the rider’s eye height.
mirrors.does: Lets you see traffic behind you.

steps: Remove the seat and the side cover.
Disconnect the negative (black) terminal first.
Install the new battery. Reconnect the positive first.
battery.signs: Slow cranking, dim lights, or a swollen case.
battery.where: Under the seat, behind the side cover on the frame. It is hidden, so lift the seat and look for the box with two terminals.
battery.does: Starts the engine and powers the lights and horn.
